lympho, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.
lympha
.
To water, dilute with water: admixto vino lymphato, id est, aqua temperato,.—
To drive out of one's senses, to distract with fear, to make mad: urbem,: urbes incursibus,: hac herba pota lymphari homines,. —As neutr.: lymphantes animi,driven crazy, mad,.—Hence, lymphātus, a, um, P. a., distracted, crazy, beside one's self, mad: exercitum pavor invasit: quippe lymphati trepidare coeperunt,: lymphati et attoniti,: repente lymphati destrictis gladiis invadunt,: lymphatis caeco pavore animis,: sine more furit lymphata per urbem,: pectora,: mens,: urbs,: lymphato cursu ruere,.

Lydian: regna,of Gyges,: aurifer amnis,i. e. Pactolus,: mitra, (4, 16), 30: pensa,which Omphale gave to Hercules,: nurus,i. e. Omphale,: sil. : lapis, a touchstone (at first found only on the Tmolus), : moduli,.—

Lўcāon, ŏnis, m., = Λυκάων,

His grandson, also called Arcas, .—Hence,
Lўcāŏnĭus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to Lycaon, Lycaonian: mensa,: parens,i. e. Callisto,; cf. : Arctos,i. e. Callisto as the constellation of the Bear,; . —Hence, axis, the northern sky, where the constellation of the Bear is situated, .—
Lўcāŏnis, ĭdis, f., the daughter of Lycaon, i. e. Callisto, .

la:other:Lycurgus.html:
Lўcurgus, i, m., = Λυκοῦργος.
Son of Dryas, king of the Edones, who prohibited the worship of Bacchus to his subjects, and ordered all the vines to be destroyed, ; ; ; ; ; .—
Son of Pheres, a king of Nemea, . —
Son of Aleus and Neæra, and father of Ancæus, a king of Arcadia; hence, Lў-curgīdes, ae, m., a male descendant of Lycurgus, i. e. Ancæus, ; and: Lўcŏorgīdes, ae, m., the same, P.—
The famous lawgiver of the Spartans, ; ; sq.; ; et saep.—
An Athenian orator, the contemporary and friend of Demosthenes, famed for his incorruptible integrity, ; .—Transf., for a severe magistrate: Lycurgos invenisse se praedicabat et Cassios, columina justitiae prisca,.—Hence, Lўcur-gēi, ōrum, m., = Λυκούργειοι, disciples of Lycurgus, inflexibly severe: nosmetipsi, qui Lycurgei a principio fuissemus, cotidie demitigamur,.
